pp:ec:2015:q1.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 1
pp:ec:2015:q1.question:
Consider a system of linear equations:
x - 2 y + 3z = -1,
x - 3y + 4z = 1, and
-2x + 4 y - 6z = k.
The value of k for which the system has infinitely many solutions is ______.

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} x-2 y+3 z&=-1 \\ x-3 y+1 z&=1, \text { and } \\ -2 x+1 y-6 z&= k \\ \left[A:B \right]&=\left[\begin{array}{rrrrr} 1 & -2 & 3 :& -1 \\ 1 & -3 & 4 :& 1 \\ -2 & 4 & 6 :& k \end{array}\right]\\ R_{2} \rightarrow R_{2}-R_{1}, R_{3} &\rightarrow R_{1}+2 R_{1} \\ \left[\begin{array}{cccc} 1 & -2 & 3 :& -1 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 :& 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 :& k-2 \end{array}\right] \end{aligned}$$

For Infinlto may solulion

$$\begin{aligned} \rho(A: B)&=p(A)\\ &= r \lt  \text{ number of variables}\\ \rho(A: B)&=2 \\ k-2&=0 \\ k&=2 \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **2**.

pp:ec:2015:q2.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 2
pp:ec:2015:q2.question: A function $f(x) =1- x^{2}+x^{3}$ is defined in the closed interval [-1,1]. The value of x , in the open interval (-1,1) for which the mean value theorem is satisfied, is

detailed_solution.markdown:
Since $f(1)\neq f(-1)$ Rolle's mean value theorem does not apply

By Lagrange moon voluo theorem

$$\begin{aligned} f^{\prime}(x) &=\frac{((1)-f(-1)}{1-(-1)}=\frac{2}{2}=1 \\ -2 x+3 x^{2} &=1 \\ x &=1-\frac{1}{3}\\ x \text{ lies in }(-1,1) \\ \Rightarrow \quad x&=-\frac{1}{3} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

pp:ec:2015:q3.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 3
pp:ec:2015:q3.question: Suppose A and B are two independent events with probabilities $P(A) \neq 0$ and $P(B) \neq 0$. Let $\bar{A}$ and $\bar{B}$ be their complements. Which one of the following statements is FALSE?

detailed_solution.markdown:
$P(A \cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A \cap B)$

since $P(A \cap B)=P(A) \rho(B)$

(not necessarily equal to zero).

So, $P(A \cup B)=P(A)+P(B)$ is false.

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ec:2015:q13.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 13
pp:ec:2015:q13.question: In the circuit shown, the switch SW is thrown from position A to position B at time t = 0. The energy (in $\mu$J) taken from the 3 V source to charge the 0.1 $\mu$F capacitor from 0 V to 3 V is

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} v_{c}\left(0^{-}\right) &=0 \mathrm{V} \\ v_{c}\left(0^{+}\right) &=0 \mathrm{V} \\ v_{c}(\infty) &=3 \mathrm{V}\\ \text{Time constant,}\\ \tau &=\mathrm{RC}=120 \times 0.1 \times 10^{-6} \\ \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{c}}(t) &=3+(0-3) e^{-t / \tau} \\ &=3\left(1-e^{-t / \tau}\right) \\ I_{\mathrm{c}}(t) &=\frac{\mathrm{Cd} v_{\mathrm{c}}(t)}{d t}=\frac{0.1 \times 10^{-6} \times 3 \times e^{-t / \tau}}{\tau} \\ &=\frac{0.1 \times 10^{-6} \times 3 e^{-t / \tau}}{120 \times 0.1 \times 10^{-6}} \\ &=\frac{1}{40} e^{-t / \tau} \\ \text { Energy } &=\int_{0}^{\infty} V_{I} d t \\ &=\left.\int_{0}^{\infty} 3 \cdot \frac{1}{40} \times e^{-t / \tau} \\ & =-\frac{3}{40} \times \tau e^{-t / \tau} \right|_{0}^{\infty}\\ &=\frac{3}{40} \times 12 \times 10^{-6}=0.9 \mu \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ec:2015:q20.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 20
pp:ec:2015:q20.question: A unity negative feedback system has the open-loop transfer function $G(s)=\frac{K}{s(s+1)(s+3)}$. The value of the gain K ($\gt$0) at which the root locus crosses the imaginary axis is ________.

detailed_solution.markdown:
$G(s)=\frac{K}{s(s+1)(s+3)}$

The characteristic equation

$$\begin{array}{l} =1+G(s) H(s)=0 \\ =s(s+1)(s+3)+K=0 \\ =s^{3}+4 s^{2}+3 s+K=0 \end{array}$$

Using Routh's tabular form

$$\begin{array}{c|cc} s^{3} & 1 & 3 \\ s^{2} & 4 & K \\ s^{1} & \frac{12-K}{4} & 0 \\ s^{0} & K & \end{array}$$

In order to cross the imaginary axis, system

should be marginally stable

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{12-K}{4}&=0\\ \text{or }\quad K&=12 \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **12**.

pp:ec:2015:q25.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 25
pp:ec:2015:q25.question: The electric field component of a plane wave traveling in a lossless dielectric medium is given by $\vec{E}(z,t)=\hat{a_{y}}2cos(10^{8}t-\frac{z}{\sqrt{2}})V/m$. The wavelength (in m) for the wave is ___________.

detailed_solution.markdown:
$\vec{E}(z, t)=\hat{a}_{y} 2 \cos \left(10^{8} t-\frac{z}{\sqrt{2}}\right) \mathrm{V} / \mathrm{m}$

General form of

$\vec{E}(z, t)=\hat{a}_{y} E_{o} \cos (\omega t-\beta z) \vee / m$

Comparing both, we get $\beta=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

since, $\beta=\frac{2 \pi}{\lambda}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **8.885** (acceptable range: [8.85, 8.92]).

pp:ec:2015:q26.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 26
pp:ec:2015:q26.question: The solution of the differential equation $\frac{d^{2}y}{dt^{2}}+2\frac{dy}{dt}+y=0\;  with \;  y(0)={y}'(0)=1$ is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} \left(D^{2}+2 D+1\right) &=0 \\ D &=-1,-1 \\ y(t) &=\left(C_{1}+C_{2} t\right) e^{-t} \\ y(t) &=C_{2} e^{-t}+\left(C_{1}+C_{2} t\right)\left(-e^{-t}\right) \\ y(0) &=y^{\prime}(0)=1 \\ \text { From here, } C_{1} &=1, C_{2}=2 \\ \Rightarrow \quad\quad y(t) &=(1+2 t) e^{-t} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

pp:ec:2015:q27.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 27
pp:ec:2015:q27.question: A vector $\vec{P}$ is given by $\vec{P}=x^{3}y \vec{a}_{x}-x^{2}y^{2} \vec{a}_{y}-x^{2}yz \hat{a}_{z}$. Which one of the following statements is TRUE?

detailed_solution.markdown:
$\vec{P}=x^{3} y \vec{a}_{x}-x^{2} y^{2} \vec{a}_{y}-x^{2} y z \vec{a}_{z}$

For solenoidal, $\nabla \cdot \vec{P}=0$

$$\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \nabla \cdot \vec{P} &=\frac{\partial P_{r}}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial P_{y}}{\partial y}+\frac{\partial P_{z}}{\partial z} \\ &=3 r^{2} y-2 r^{2} y-x^{2} y \\ &=0 \end{aligned}$$

$\Rightarrow \vec{P}$ is solenoidal

For irrotational, $\nabla \times \vec{P}=0$

$$\Rightarrow \nabla \times \vec{P}=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\vec{a}_{x} & \vec{a}_{y} & \vec{a}_{z} \\ \frac{\partial}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial}{\partial z} \\ x^{3} y & -x^{2} y^{2} & -x^{2} y z\end{array}\right|$$

$=\vec{a}_{x}\left(-x^{2} z\right)+\vec{a}_{y}(2 x y z)+\vec{a}_{z}\left(-2 x^{2}-x^{3}\right)$

$\neq 0$

$\Rightarrow \vec{P}$ is not irrotational.

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ec:2015:q28.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 28
pp:ec:2015:q28.question: Which one of the following graphs describes the function $f(x)=e^{-x}(x^{2}+x+1)$?

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} f(x) &=e^{-x}\left(x^{2}+x+1\right) \\ f^{\prime}(x) &=e^{-x}(2 x+1)-e^{-x}\left(x^{2}+x+1\right) \\ &=e^{-x}\left(x-x^{2}\right)=e^{-x}(x)(1-x) \end{aligned}$$

Putting $f^{\prime}(x)=0,$ we get

$$\begin{aligned} x &=0 \text { or } x=1 \\ f^{\prime \prime}(x) &=e^{-x}(1-2 x)-\theta^{-x}\left(x-x^{2}\right) \\ &=e^{-x}\left(1-3 x+x^{2}\right)\\ \text{At }x&=0, f^{\prime \prime}(x)=1 \text{ (so we have a minimum).}\\ \text{At }x&=1, f^{\prime \prime}(x)=-\frac{1}{e} \\ &\quad \quad\text{(so we have a maximum).}\\ \end{aligned}$$

Only curve (b) slows a single local minimum at x=0 and a single local maximum at x=1

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

pp:ec:2015:q29.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 29
pp:ec:2015:q29.question: The maximum area (in square units) of a rectangle whose vertices lie on the ellipse $x^{2}+4y^{2}=1$ is_______.

detailed_solution.markdown: $x^{2}+4 y^{2}=1$ Area of rectangle $$\begin{aligned} &=2 x \cdot 2 y=4 x y\\ \text { Let } \quad &=(\text { Area })^{2} \\ &=16 x^{2} y^{2} \\ &=4 x^{2}\left(1-x^{2}\right) \quad\left(\because 1-x^{2}=4 y^{2}\right) \\ f^{\prime}(x) &=0 \\ \frac{d}{d x}\left[4\left(x^{2}-x^{4}\right)\right] &=0 \\ 4\left(2 x-4 x^{3}\right) &=0\\ \text{We get, }\quad x&=\pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ y &=\pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{8}} \\ \text { Area } &=4 x y=4 \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{8}}=1 \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **1** (acceptable range: [0.95, 1.05]).

pp:ec:2015:q31.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 31
pp:ec:2015:q31.question: In the circuit shown, switch SW is closed at t = 0. Assuming zero initial conditions, the value of $v_{c}(t)$ (in Volts) at t = 1 sec is ________.

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} & v_{c}\left(0^{-}\right)=0 \mathrm{V} \\ & v_{c}\left(0^{+}\right)=0 \mathrm{V} \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned} v_{c}(\infty)&=\frac{2}{2+3} \times 10 \\ &=4 \mathrm{V}[\text { By voltage divider }] \\ v_{c}(t)&=4\left[1-e^{-t / \tau}\right] \\ \tau &=R_{\mathrm{eq}} C=\frac{3 \times 2}{3+2} \times \frac{5}{6} \\ &=1 \mathrm{sec} \\ v_{c}(1) &=4\left[1-e^{-1 / 1}\right]=2.528 \mathrm{Volts} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **2.53** (acceptable range: [2.48, 2.58]).

pp:ec:2015:q32.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 32
pp:ec:2015:q32.question: In the given circuit, the maximum power (in Watts) that can be transferred to the load $R_{L}$ is_______.

detailed_solution.markdown: For maximum power transfer $$\begin{aligned} R_{L} &=\left|Z_{T h}\right|=|2 \| j 2| \\ &=\left|\frac{2 \times j 2}{2+j 2}\right|=1.414 \Omega \\ V_{T h} &=\frac{8 \angle 90^{\circ}}{2+j 2}=2.828 \angle 45^{\circ} \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned} I &=\frac{2.828 \angle 45^{\circ}}{1.414 \angle 45^{\circ}+1.414}=1.08 \angle 22.5^{\circ} \\ \text { Power } &=I^{2} R=(1.08)^{2} \times \sqrt{2}=1.649 \mathrm{W} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **1.65** (acceptable range: [1.6, 1.7]).

pp:ec:2015:q33.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 33
pp:ec:2015:q33.question: The built-in potential of an abrupt p-n junction is 0.75 V. If its junction capacitance $(C_{J})$ at a reverse bias $(V_{R})$ of 1.25 V is 5 pF, the value of $C_{J}$ (in pF) when $V_{R}$ = 7.25 V is ________.

detailed_solution.concept: Electronic Devices - PN-Junction Diodes and Special Diodes
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} C_{j} &\propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{V_{b i}+V_{R}}} \\ \frac{C_{2 j}}{C_{1 j}}&=\sqrt{\frac{V_{b i}+V_{R_{1}}}{V_{b i}+V_{R_{2}}}} \\ C_{2 j}&=C_{1 j} \sqrt{\frac{2}{8}}=\frac{C_{1 j}}{2}=2.5 \mathrm{pF} \end{aligned}$$

So, answer is 2.5

Therefore, the correct answer is **2.5** (acceptable range: [2.4, 2.6]).

pp:ec:2015:q34.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 34
pp:ec:2015:q34.question: A MOSFET in saturation has a drain current of 1 mA for $V_{DS} = 0.5$ V. If the channel length modulation coefficient is 0.05 $V^{-1}$, the output resistance (in   $k\Omega$) of the MOSFET is _________.

detailed_solution.concept: Electronic Devices - BJT and FET Basics
detailed_solution.markdown:
Under channel length modulation,

$$\begin{aligned} I_{D}&=I_{\text {Dsat }}\left(1+\lambda V_{\text {DS }}\right)\\ \frac{d I_{D}}{d V_{D S}} &=\frac{1}{r_{0}}=\lambda I_{\text {Dsat }} \\ r_{O} &=\frac{1}{\lambda I_{D \text { sat }}}=\frac{1}{0.05 \times 10^{-3}}=20 \mathrm{k} \Omega \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **20** (acceptable range: [19, 21]).

pp:ec:2015:q35.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 35
pp:ec:2015:q35.question:
For a silicon diode with long P and N regions, the accepter and donor impurity concentrations are $1 \times 10^{17} cm^{-3}$ and $1 \times 10^{15} cm^{-3}$, respectively. The lifetimes of electrons in P region and holes in N region are both 100 $\mu s$. The electron and hole diffusion coefficients are $49 cm^{2}/s \; and \; 36 cm^{2}/s$,
respectively. Assume kT/q = 26 mV, the intrinsic carrier concentration is $1 \times 10^{10} cm^{-3}, \; and \;  q = 1.6 \times  10^{-19}$ C. When a forward voltage of 208 mV is applied across the diode, the hole current density (in nA/$cm^{2}$) injected from P region to N region is _____________.

detailed_solution.concept: Electronic Devices - PN-Junction Diodes and Special Diodes
detailed_solution.markdown:
The hole current density injected from P region to N region is given by

$\frac{q n_{i}^{2} D_{p}}{N_{D} L_{p}}\left[\exp \left(\frac{V_{F B}}{\eta V_{T}}\right)-1\right]$

where,

q= charge on electron

$n_{i}=$ Intrinsic carrier concentration in silicon

$N_{D}=$ Donor doping

$D_{p}=$ Hole diffusion coefficient

$L_{p}=$ Mean diffusion length of hole

$V_{F B}=$ Forward voltage applied across diode

$$\begin{aligned} V_{T}=& k T / q=26 \mathrm{mV} \\ L_{p} &=\sqrt{\tau_{p} D_{p}}=\sqrt{100 \times 10^{-6} \times 36} \\ &=0.06 \mathrm{cm} \end{aligned}$$

Using the above values, we get hole current  density injected from P region to N region

Therefore, the correct answer is **29** (acceptable range: [28, 30]).

pp:ec:2015:q36.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 36
pp:ec:2015:q36.question: The Boolean expression $f(X,Y,Z)=\bar{X}Y\bar{Z}+X\bar{Y}\bar{Z}+XY\bar{Z}+XYZ$ converted into the canonical product of sum (POS) form is

detailed_solution.markdown: $F(X, Y, Z)=\bar{X} Y \bar{Z}+X \overline{Y Z}+X Y \bar{Z}+X Y Z$ $F=(X+Y+Z)(X+Y+\bar{Z})(X+\bar{Y}+\bar{Z})(\bar{X}+Y+\bar{Z})$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ec:2015:q37.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 37
pp:ec:2015:q37.question: All the logic gates shown in the figure have a propagation delay of 20 ns. Let A = C = 0 and B = 1 until time t = 0. At t = 0, all the inputs flip (i.e., A = C = 1 and B = 0) and remain in that state. For t > 0, output Z = 1 for a duration (in ns) of ______________.

detailed_solution.markdown: Z is '1' for 40 n-sec. Therefore, the correct answer is **40**.

pp:ec:2015:q38.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 38
pp:ec:2015:q38.question: A 3-input majority gate is defined by the logic function M(a,b,c) = ab + bc + ca . Which one of the following gates is represented by the function  $M(M\overline{(a,b,c)},M(a,b,\bar{c}),c)$ ?

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} M(a, b, c) &=a b+b c+c a \\ \overline{M(a, b, c)} &=\frac{a b+b c+c a}{a b \cdot b c} \cdot \overline{c a} \\ &=(\bar{a}+\bar{b})(\bar{b}+\bar{c})(\bar{c}+\bar{a}) \\ M(a, b, \bar{c}) &=a b+b \bar{c}+\bar{c} a \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{array}{l} \begin{aligned} M(\overline{M(a, b, c)}, M(a, b, \bar{c}) c) &=\\ \left[\begin{array}{l}(\overline{a b} \cdot \overline{b c} \cdot \overline{c a})(a b+b \bar{c}+\overline{c a}) \\ +(a b+b \bar{c}+\bar{c} a)(c)+(\overline{a b} \cdot \overline{b c} \cdot \bar{a} a \mid)\end{array}\right]\end{aligned} \\ =\left[\begin{array}{l} (\bar{a}+\bar{b})(\bar{b}+\bar{c})(\bar{c}+\bar{a})(a b+b \bar{c}+\bar{c} a) \\ +a b c+(\bar{a}+\bar{b})(\bar{b}+\bar{c})(\bar{c}+\bar{a}) c \end{array}\right] \\ =(\bar{a}+\bar{b})(\bar{b}+\bar{c})(\bar{c}+\bar{a})[a b+b \bar{c}+\bar{c} a+c]+a b c \\ =(\bar{a}+\bar{b})(\bar{b}+\bar{c})(\bar{c}+\bar{a})[a+b+c]+a b c \\ =(\bar{a} \bar{b}+\bar{b} \bar{c}+\bar{c} \bar{a})[a+b+c]+a b c \\ F=a \bar{b} \bar{c}+b \bar{c} \bar{a}+c \bar{a} \bar{b}+a b c \\ F=A \oplus B \oplus C \end{array}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

pp:ec:2015:q39.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 39
pp:ec:2015:q39.question: For the NMOSFET in the circuit shown, the threshold voltage is $V_{th}$ , where $V_{th}$ > 0. The source voltage $V_{SS}$ is varied from 0 to $V_{DD}$. Neglecting the channel length modulation, the drain current $I_{D}$ as a function of $V_{SS}$ is represented by

$V_{G S}=V_{D S}$

pp:ec:2015:q40.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 40
pp:ec:2015:q40.question: In the circuit shown, assume that the opamp is ideal. The bridge output voltage $V_{0}$ (in mV) for $\delta$ = 0.05 is _______.

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} I_{50 \Omega} &=\frac{1}{50} A=I_{100 \Omega} \\ V_{0} &=\frac{1}{100}[250(1+\delta)-250(1-\delta)] \\ &=\frac{1}{1000} \times 250=0.25 \mathrm{V}=250 \mathrm{mV} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **250** (acceptable range: [249, 251]).

pp:ec:2015:q41.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 41
pp:ec:2015:q41.question: The circuit shown in the figure has an ideal opamp. The oscillation frequency and the condition to sustain the oscillations, respectively, are

detailed_solution.markdown:
Frequency of Wein bridge oscillator is $\omega_{0} =\frac{1}{R C}$

but in the question time constant is double so

frequency becomes half.

$$\begin{aligned} \omega_{0} &=\frac{1}{2 R C} \\ Z_{1} &=2 R+\frac{1}{j \omega C}=2(R-j R) \\ Z_{2} &=\frac{R \times \frac{1}{2 j \omega C}}{R+\frac{1}{2 j \omega C}}=\frac{\frac{R^{2}}{j}}{R-j R} \\ \beta &=\frac{Z_{2}}{Z_{1}+Z_{2}}=\frac{1}{5} \\ 1+\frac{R_{1}}{R_{2}}&=5 \quad \Rightarrow R_{1}=4 R_{2} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

pp:ec:2015:q42.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 42
pp:ec:2015:q42.question: In the circuit shown, $I_{1}$ = 80 mA and $I_{2}$ = 4 mA. Transistors $T_{1} \; and \; T_{2}$ are identical. Assume that the thermal voltage $V_{T}$ is 26 mV at $27^{\circ}C$. At $50^{\circ}C$, the value of the voltage $V_{12} = V_{1} -V_{2}$ (in mV) is_______.

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} I_{2} &=I_{s} e^{\frac{V_{B E_{2}}}{\eta V_{T}}} \\ V_{B E_{2}} &=V_{2} \\ I_{1} &=I_{S} e^{\frac{V_{BE_{1}}}{\eta V_{T}} } \\ V_{B E_{1}} &=V_{1} \\ \frac{I_{1}}{I_{2}} &=e^{\frac{V_{1}-V_{2}}{\eta} V_{T}} \end{aligned}$$

since, $V_{T}$ at $27^{\circ}$ is $26 \mathrm{mV}$ then $V_{T}$ at $50^{\circ}$ is $27.99 \mathrm{mV}$ Thus,

$V_{1}-V_{2}=83.15 \mathrm{mV}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **83.75** (acceptable range: [83.5, 84]).

pp:ec:2015:q43.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 43
pp:ec:2015:q43.question:
Two sequences [a,b,c] and [A,B,C] are related as
$$\begin{bmatrix} A\\ B\\ C \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1& 1\\ 1& W_{3}^{-1} & W_{3}^{-2}\\ 1&W_{3}^{-2} & W_{3}^{-4} \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} a\\ b\\ c \end{bmatrix} \; where\; W_{3}=e^{j\frac{2\pi }{3}}$$
If another sequence [ p, q, r] is derived as,
$$\begin{bmatrix} p\\ q\\ r \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1& 1\\ 1& W_{3}^{1} & W_{3}^{2}\\ 1&W_{3}^{2} & W_{3}^{4} \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0\\ 0 & W_{3}^{2} &0 \\ 0&0 & W_{3}^{4} \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} A/3\\ B/3\\ C/3\end{bmatrix}$$
then the relationship between the sequences [ p, q, r] and [a, b, c] is

detailed_solution.concept: Signals and Systems - DTFS, DTFT and DFT
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} \left[\begin{array}{l}A \\ B \\ C\end{array}\right]&=\left[\begin{array}{l}a+b+c \\ a+b W_{3}^{-1}+c W_{3}^{-2} \\ a+b W_{3}^{-2}+c W_{3}^{-1}\end{array}\right] \\ \left[\begin{array}{l}p \\ q \\ r\end{array}\right]&=\left[\begin{array}{ccc}1 & w_{3}^{2} & w_{3}^{1} \\ 1 & w_{3}^{1} w_{3}^{2} & w_{3}^{2} w_{3}^{1} \\ 1 & w_{3}^{2} w_{3}^{2} & W_{3}^{1} W_{3}^{1}\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{c}\frac{a+b+c}{3} \\ \frac{a+b W_{3}^{-1}+c W_{3}^{2}}{3} \\ \frac{a+b W_{3}^{-2}+c W_{3}^{-1}}{3}\end{array}\right] \\ \text{where }&\quad W_{3}^{4}=e^{i \frac{2 \pi}{3}} \\ &\quad W_{3}^{2}=e^{i \frac{4 \pi}{3}}\\ W_{3}^{-1}&=e^{-j \frac{2 \pi}{3}} \\ W_{3}^{-2}&=e^{-j \frac{4 \pi}{3}} \\ W_{3}^{-4}&=W_{3}^{-1}=e^{-j \frac{2 \pi}{3}} \\ \left[\begin{array}{l}p \\q \\r\end{array}\right]&=\left[\begin{array}{l} c \\a \\b\end{array}\right] \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ec:2015:q44.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 44
pp:ec:2015:q44.question: For the discrete-time system shown in the figure, the poles of the system transfer function are located at

detailed_solution.markdown:
The difference equation of the system

$x(n)-\frac{1}{6} y(n-2)+\frac{5}{6} y(n-1)=y(n)$

$$H(z)=\begin{array}{l}Y(z) \\ x(z)\end{array}=\frac{1}{1+\frac{1}{6} z^{-2}-\frac{5}{6} z^{-1}}$$

$Poles are at z=\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{3}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ec:2015:q45.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 45
pp:ec:2015:q45.question: The pole-zero diagram of a causal and stable discrete-time system is shown in the figure. The zero at the origin has multiplicity 4. The impulse response of the system is h[n]. If h[0] = 1, we canconclude
options: h[n] is real for all n
h[n] is purely imaginary for all n
h[n] is real for only even n
h[n] is purely imaginary for only odd n

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} H(z) &=\frac{z^{4}}{\left[\left(z-\frac{1}{2}\right)^{2}+\frac{1}{4}\right]\left[\left(z+\frac{1}{2}\right)^{2}+\frac{1}{4}\right]} \\ \text { Poles } &=\frac{1}{2} \pm j \frac{1}{2},-\frac{1}{2} \pm j \frac{1}{2} \\ &=\frac{z^{4}}{\left(z^{2}-z+\frac{1}{2}\right)\left(z^{2}+z+\frac{1}{2}\right)} \\ &=\frac{z^{4}}{z^{4}+z^{2}+\frac{1}{4}-z^{2}}\\ H(z)&=\frac{z^{4}}{z^{4}+\frac{1}{4}} \\ &\left.=z^{4}+\frac{1}{4}\right) z^{4}\left(1-\frac{1}{4} z^{-4} \cdots\right.\\ &\quad \quad \frac{z+\frac{1}{4}}{-\frac{1}{4}} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ec:2015:q46.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 46
pp:ec:2015:q46.question: The open-loop transfer function of a plant in a unity feedback configuration is given as $G(s)=\frac{K(s+4)}{(s+8)(s^{2}-9)}$ . The value of the gain K(> 0) for which -1+ j2 lies on the root locus is_______.

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} G(s) &=\frac{K(s+4)}{(s+8)\left(s^{2}-9\right)} \\ &=\frac{K(s+4)}{(s+8)(s+3)(s-3)} \end{aligned}$$

For the point (-1+2 j) to lie on the root locus the angle condition must be satisfy

i.e. $\angle G(s) H(s)=\pm(2 Q+1) 180^{\circ}$

Taking LHS:

$$\begin{array}{l} \left.\angle G(s) H(s)\right|_{s=-1+2 j} \\ =\frac{\angle K+\angle(s+4)}{\angle(s+8)+\angle(s+3)+\angle(s-3)} \\ =\frac{\angle K+\angle(-1+2 j+4)}{\angle(-1+2 j+8)+\angle(-1+2 j+3)+\angle(-1+2 j-3)} \\ =\frac{0+\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)}{\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{7}\right)+\tan ^{-1}(1)+180^{\circ}-\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)} \\ =33.69^{\circ}-15.945^{\circ}-45^{\circ}-180^{\circ}+26.565^{\circ} \\ \simeq 180^{\circ} \end{array}$$

As angle condition is satisfied the value of system gain K can be obtained by using magnitude

condition

$$\begin{array}{l} i.e. |G(s) H(s)|_{s=-1+2 j}=1 \\ =\frac{K \sqrt{(-1+4)^{2}+2^{2}}}{\sqrt{(-1+8)^{2}+2^{2}} \cdot \sqrt{(-1+3)^{2}+2^{2}} \cdot \sqrt{(-1-3)^{2}+2^{2}}} \\ =1 \\ =\frac{K \sqrt{9+4}}{\sqrt{49+4} \sqrt{4+4} \sqrt{16+4}}=1 \\ =\frac{K \sqrt{13}}{\sqrt{53} \sqrt{8} \sqrt{20}}=1 \\ K=\frac{\sqrt{53 \times 8 \times 20}}{\sqrt{13}}=25.54 \end{array}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **25.5** (acceptable range: [25, 26]).

pp:ec:2015:q47.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 47
pp:ec:2015:q47.question: A lead compensator network includes a parallel combination of R and C in the feed-forward path. If the transfer function of the compensator is $G(s)=\frac{s+2}{s+4}$ , the value of RC is ________.

detailed_solution.markdown: $G_{C}(s)=\frac{s+2}{s+4} \quad\dots(i)$ For lead compensator, Transfer function $=\frac{1+s \tau}{1+\alpha s \tau} \quad\dots(ii)$ Where, $\tau=$ Lead time constant $=R_{1} C$ and $\alpha=\frac{R_{2}}{R_{1}+R_{2}}$ Comparing equation (i) and (ii), we get $\tau=\frac{1}{2} \quad$ and $\quad \alpha \tau=\frac{1}{4}$ or, $\alpha=\frac{1}{2}$ $\therefore$ RC time constant =0.5 Therefore, the correct answer is **0.5**.

pp:ec:2015:q48.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 48
pp:ec:2015:q48.question: A plant transfer function is given as $G(s)=(K_{P}+\frac{K_{I}}{s})\frac{1}{s(s+2)}$. When the plant operates in a unity feedback configuration, the condition for the stability of the closed loop system is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$G(s)=\left(K_{p}+\frac{K_{I}}{s}\right)\left(\frac{1}{s(s+2)}\right)$

The closed loop transfer function for unity feedback

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{G(s)}{1+G(s)} &=\frac{\left(K_{p} s+K_{I}\right)}{s^{2}(s+2)+\left(K_{p} s+K_{I}\right)} \\ &=\frac{K_{p} s+K_{I}}{s^{3}+2 s^{2}+K_{p} s+K_{I}} \end{aligned}$$

Using Routh's tabular form:

$$\begin{array}{c|cc} s^{3} & 1 & K_{p} \\ s^{2} & 2 & K_{I} \\ s^{1} & \frac{2 K_{p}-K_{I}}{2} & 0 \\ s^{0} & K_{p} & \end{array}$$

For system to be stable;

$$\begin{aligned} K_{p}& \gt 0\\ \text{and }\frac{2 K_{p}-K_{I}}{2}& \gt 0 \\ \text{or} \quad 2 K_{p}-K_{I}& \gt 0 \\ \text{or} \quad K_{p}& \gt \frac{K_{I}}{2} \gt 0 \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ec:2015:q49.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 49
pp:ec:2015:q49.question: The input X to the Binary Symmetric Channel (BSC) shown in the figure is ' 1' with probability 0.8.The cross-over probability is 1/7. If the received bit Y = 0, the conditional probability that '1' was transmitted is _______.

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{array}{l} P(X=1 / Y=0) \\ =\frac{P(Y=0 / X=1) P(X=1)}{P(Y=0 / X=1) P(X=1)+P(Y=0 / X=0) P(X=0)} \\ =\frac{\left(\frac{1}{7}\right)(0.8)}{\left(\frac{1}{7}\right)(0.8)+\left(\frac{6}{7}\right)(0.2)}=0.4 \end{array}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **0.4** (acceptable range: [0.39, 0.41]).

pp:ec:2015:q51.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 51
pp:ec:2015:q51.question: In the system shown in Figure (a), m(t) is a low-pass signal with bandwidth W Hz. The frequency response of the band-pass filter H(f) is shown in Figure (b). If it is desired that the output signal z(t) = 10x(t), the maximum value of W (in Hz) should be strictly less than ________.

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{array}{l} \quad x(t)=m(t) \cos 2400 \pi t \\ \text { thus } \quad y(t)=10 x(t)+x^{2}(t) \\ \therefore y(t)=10 m(t) \cos (2400 \pi t)+m^{2}(t) \cos ^{2}(2400 \pi t) \\ =10 m(t) \cos (2400 \pi t)+\frac{1}{2} m^{2}(t) \frac{1}{2} \cos (4800 \pi t) \end{array}$$ Drawing the spectrum set spectrum of x(t) be $y(t) = 10x(t) + x^{2}(t)$ To recover z(t) $$\begin{aligned} 1200-W \gt 700 & \Rightarrow W \lt 500 \\ 1200+W \lt 1700 & \Rightarrow W \lt 500 \\ 2 W \lt 700 & \Rightarrow W \lt 350 \\ 2400-2 W \gt 1700 & \Rightarrow W \lt 350 \end{aligned}$$ So, that maximum value of W should be less than 350 Hz Therefore, the correct answer is **349.5** (acceptable range: [349, 350]).

pp:ec:2015:q52.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 52
pp:ec:2015:q52.question:
A source emits bit 0 with probability 1/3 and bit 1 with probability 2/3. The emitted bits are communicated to the receiver. The receiver decides for either 0 or 1 based on the received value R . It is given that the conditional density functions of R are as
$$f_{(R|0)}(r)=\left\{\begin{matrix} \frac{1}{4}, & -3\leq x\leq 1,\\ 0, & otherwise, \end{matrix}\right.$$ and

$$f_{(R|1)}(r)=\left\{\begin{matrix} \frac{1}{6}, &-1\leq x\leq 5, \\ 0,& otherwise. \end{matrix}\right.$$
The minimum decision error probability is

detailed_solution.markdown: According to MAP criteria, for optimum threshold, $f_{R}\left(r \mid s_{0}\right) P\left(s_{0}\right) \sum_{k_{1}}^{r_{0}} f_{B}\left(r \mid s_{1}\right) P\left(s_{1}\right)$ Given that, $P\left(s_{0}\right)=\frac{1}{3} \text { and } P\left(s_{1}\right)=\frac{2}{3}$ From the above figure, it is clear that, $$\begin{array}{l} f_{B}\left(r \mid s_{0}\right) P\left(s_{0}\right)>f_{R}\left(r \mid s_{1}\right) P\left(s_{1}\right) \Rightarrow \text { for } r<-1 \\ f_{A}\left(r \mid s_{1}\right) P\left(s_{1}\right)>f_{R}\left(r \mid s_{0}\right) P\left(s_{0}\right) \Rightarrow \text { for } r>-1 \end{array}$$ So, optimum threshold will be, $r_{\mathrm{th}}=-1$ $$\begin{aligned} \text{ For }r_{\mathrm{th}}=-1& \\ P\left(r_{0} \mid s_{1}\right) P\left(s_{1}\right)&=0\\ P\left(r_{1} \mid s_{0}\right) P\left(s_{0}\right)&=\frac{1}{12}[1-(-1)]=\frac{1}{6} \\ P_{e(\mathrm{min})}&=P\left(r_{0} \mid s_{1}\right) P\left(s_{1}\right)+P\left(q \mid s_{0}\right) P\left(s_{0}\right)=\frac{1}{6} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

pp:ec:2015:q53.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 53
pp:ec:2015:q53.question:
The longitudinal component of the magnetic field inside an air-filled rectangular waveguide made of a perfect electric conductor is given by the following expression
$H_{z}(x,y,z,t)=0.1 cos(25\pi x) cos(30.3 \pi y)$ $cos(12 \pi *10^{9}t-\beta z) (A/m)$
The cross-sectional dimensions of the waveguide are given as a = 0.08 m and b = 0.033 m. The mode of propagation inside the waveguide is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} H_{z}(x, y, z, t) &=0.1 \cos (25 \pi x) \cos (30.3 \pi y) \\ & \cos \left(12 \pi \times 10^{9} t-\beta z\right)^{-1 / m}\\ a &=0.08 m, b=0.033 m \end{aligned}$$

Axial component is $\mathrm{H} \Rightarrow$ the propagating mode is

$T E_{\text {mn}}$, m, n can be found by

$$\begin{array}{l} \quad \frac{m \pi}{a} x=25 \pi x \\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{m}{0.08}=25 \\ \Rightarrow \quad m=2 \\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{n\pi}{b} y=30.3 \pi y \\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{n}{0.033}=30.3 \\ \Rightarrow \quad n=1 \end{array}$$

$\therefore$ The mode of propagation is $T E_{21}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ec:2015:q54.title: GATE EC 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 54
pp:ec:2015:q54.question:
The electric field intensity of a plane wave traveling in free space is given by the following expression
$E(x,t)=a_{y}24\pi cos(\omega t-k_{0}x)(V/m)$
In this field, consider a square area 10 cm x 10 cm on a plane x + y = 1. The total time-averaged power (in mW) passing through the square area is _______.

detailed_solution.markdown:
$\vec{E}(x, t)=\hat{a}_{y} 24 \pi \cos \left(\omega t-K_{o} x\right) V / m$

Power density

$\vec{P}=\frac{1}{2} \frac{|E|^{2}}{\eta}=\frac{1}{2} \frac{(24 \pi)^{2}}{120 \pi} \hat{a}_{x}$

Time-averaged power

$$\begin{aligned} P_{\mathrm{avg}} &=\vec{P} \cdot \overrightarrow{d s} \\ &=\left[\frac{1}{2} \frac{(24 \pi)^{2}}{120 \pi} \hat{a}_{x}\right] \cdot\left[\frac{\hat{a}_{x}+\hat{a}_{y}}{\sqrt{2}} \times 10^{-2}\right] \\ P_{\mathrm{avg}} &=\frac{24 \pi}{\sqrt{2}}=53.29 \mathrm{mW} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **53.5** (acceptable range: [53, 54]).

pp:ec:2015:q55.question:
Consider a uniform plane wave with amplitude $(E_{0})$ of 10 V/m and 1.1 GHz frequency travelling in air, and incident normally on a dielectric medium with complex relative permittivity ($\varepsilon_{r}$) and permeability ($\mu_{r}$) as shown in the figure.

The magnitude of the transmitted electric field component (in V/m) after it has travelled a distance of 10 cm inside the dielectric region is_________.

detailed_solution.markdown:
Material has $\mu_{R}$ and $\epsilon_{R}$ complex.

$\eta \text { of material }=\sqrt{\frac{j \omega \mu}{\sigma+j \omega \epsilon}}=\sqrt{\frac{\mu_{o} \mu_{R}}{\epsilon_{o} \epsilon_{R}}}=120 \pi$

where, $\sigma=0 \quad$ (dielectric)

No reflections at the boundary.

$$\begin{aligned} \gamma &=\text { Propagation constant } \\ &=\sqrt{j \omega \mu_{o} \mu_{R}\left(0+j \omega \epsilon_{o} \epsilon_{R}\right)} \\ &=\sqrt{j \omega \mu_{o} \epsilon_{o}(1-j 2)} \\ &=j \omega \sqrt{\mu_{o} \epsilon_{o}}+j 2 \omega \sqrt{\mu_{o} \epsilon_{o}} \\ \alpha &=2 \omega \sqrt{\mu_{o} \epsilon_{o}}=4.6 \frac{1}{\mathrm{m}} \\ |E| &=E_{o} e^{-\alpha z} \text { with } Z=0.1 \mathrm{m} \\ |E| &=0.1 \mathrm{V} / \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **0.1** (acceptable range: [0.08, 0.12]).
